### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `updateData (4 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7f4c840e4d651abdb9434258cce9c7d85a14c797` — the merge of head `51450e766c971ee903fccf2cfb3c5b3a2188f5d7` into base `35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7f4c840e4d651abdb9434258cce9c7d85a14c797 && git checkout 7f4c840e4d651abdb9434258cce9c7d85a14c797
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893 51450e766c971ee903fccf2cfb3c5b3a2188f5d7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893 && git merge --no-ff 51450e766c971ee903fccf2cfb3c5b3a2188f5d7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35f205514ce93e1871ff2e238529d7da5423c893` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9a38b6c0296098d1b52a9c09482f3a7ed4f36483`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mention-recipient-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts (cited, read to judge; not reviewed)

Governing ruling: card comment 6523848208 (maintainer 「27703 同意」, letter A). Judged against: a response-only member on the `sys_comment` create and update answer, the requester's own request only, ids only, no reason, never stored; the edit-time mention folded into the server end; the gate's verdict reused with no second derivation of readability; the gate admits the same people as before.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the net diff implies, named right or wrong against the ruling and the live tree.

1. `CreateDataResponseSchema` and `UpdateDataResponseSchema` (`protocol.zod.ts`) gain `withheldMentions: z.array(z.string()).optional()` with one shared description. **Right.** Optional and omit-when-empty keeps every existing client's reading; `z.array(z.string())` admits ids only, so a per-user object carrying a reason is refused by the schema itself (pinned in `write-answer-withheld-mentions.test.ts`). `CloneDataResponseSchema` is untouched, as the ruling names create and update only.
2. `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/CreateDataResponse:withheldMentions` and `api/UpdateDataResponse:withheldMentions`; `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` regenerated. **Right.** Generated artefacts of 1; the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Spec property liveness` check runs are `success`.
3. `WriteObservabilityOptions.onMentionsWithheld?: (userIds: readonly string[]) => void` (`contracts/data-engine.ts`). **Right.** A function, so it cannot enter the serializable Zod bags (the same wall `onFieldsDropped` / `onValidationAdvisory` sit behind, `data-engine.test.ts` L269–315); `HookUpdateOptions` is `Omit<EngineUpdateOptions,…> & WriteObservabilityOptions`, so the hook-API bag inherits it with no type change — the `hook-api.ts` hunk is a docblock word list only, and that is the correct size of change there.
4. `ENGINE_UPDATE_OPTION_KEYS` admits `onMentionsWithheld` (`engine.ts` L719), with the drift pin in `engine-unknown-option.test.ts` naming it as the fourth contract member. **Right.** `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` is called for `find`, `findOne`, `update`, `delete`, `aggregate` and not for `insert` (read at head), so the insert path needs no allowlist line.
5. Transport: `createData` / `updateData` build a per-call `Set`, pass `onMentionsWithheld` in the engine bag, and spread `withheldMentions` only when the set is non-empty. **Right.** Read in the engine: on insert each row context is built with `input: { data, options: opCtx.options }` (L14929) where `opCtx.options` is the caller's bag verbatim (L14647), then `rowCtx.input.options = buildDriverOptions(object, ctx, optionsBase)` (L15384–15396); on by-id update `input: { id, data, options: opCtx.options }` (L16476) then `buildDriverOptions` (L16959). `buildDriverOptions` either returns `base` unchanged or `{ ...base, +driver keys }` (`engine-driver-options.ts` L164–235), so the listener survives into every `after*` context, exactly as the PHASE rule in `hook.zod.ts` L879–888 states. A nested write a hook makes calls `engine.insert` with its own bag, so its verdicts cannot reach the outer set.
6. `MentionGateInput.onWithheld?: (userId: string) => void`; `withhold()` calls it only when a resolved `userId` is present, after the log line, inside its own try/catch. **Right.** The admission computation (`candidates` → `readableIn` on source then thread → `admitted`) is byte-for-byte what `main` had; the new lines are appended to the `withhold` closure only. Same people admitted as before; no second derivation of readability anywhere in the diff.
7. `writeCommentMentions` also registered on `afterUpdate` for `sys_comment`, judging only the entries the written row's `mentions` gained over `ctx.previous`. **Right.** `previous` is bound unconditionally on the by-id branch (#7867, L16681) from `readUpdatePriorRow`, which returns every declared column (`mentions` is declared), and on the predicate branch per row via `buildPerRowAfterContexts` now that `hasHooksFor('afterUpdate','sys_comment')` is true. The existing registration pins in `audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts` filter on `before*` (L487–493) and on `afterInsert` (L577–580), so they stay green; the comment at L485–486 ("on `afterInsert`") is now stale prose in a non-`hits` file.
8. REST: `crud-routes.ts` answers `res.status(201).json(result)` / `res.json(result)` with the protocol answer verbatim (L298–304, L483–488), so the key reaches the wire with no REST change. **Right**, and the first wire consumer (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`) already reads `droppedFields` / `warnings` structurally off the answer (L4060–4070), so it can read `withheldMentions` the same way when the ui card lands.
9. Client SDK: `CreateDataResult` / `UpdateDataResult` in `packages/client/src/index.ts` (L473, L528) are hand-written mirrors headed `/** Spec: CreateDataResponseSchema */` and carry `droppedFields` and `warnings` but not `withheldMentions`. **Wrong by omission** — the typed SDK surface now lags the spec it says it mirrors. No parity gate pins it (none found under `scripts/`, `packages/lint`, `packages/spec/src`), so nothing goes red; see ④ should-fix 2.
10. Batch (`createManyData` / `batchData`), clone and flow writes do not pass the listener. **Right** — the ruling names create and update; the dev report records the gap as an out-of-scope finding with the seat as carrier.

Check runs on `9a38b6c0` (42, pages 1–2 read): **13 success** — Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, filter, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness. **7 skipped** (opt-in or matrix placeholders). **22 in_progress at review time** — Test Core 1/8–8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger / workspace, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards. **0 failure.** The verdict below judges the completed runs and the tree; a red among the in-progress families reopens it.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/27703-withheld-mentions-answer.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql` — all `minor`. **Matches what the diff publishes**: spec adds an optional response member and an optional contract member (additive); metadata-protocol answers a new optional key (additive); objectql accepts a new option key it previously refused (additive); plugin-audit gains behaviour (edit-time mention notifications, a new optional gate input) with no removed or narrowed surface. No `major` is owed: nothing is removed, no existing key changes shape, the gate admits the same set. `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/client` have no source change in the diff, so no changeset is owed for them in this PR (a follow-up that updates the client mirrors, ④ should-fix 2, owes its own). `Check Changeset` is `success`. Release-owned paths (`content/docs/releases/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md`) are untouched.

Clause-②: yes — a new served key on the data-write answer (「协议新增定 p1」), stated identically in the changeset body, the PR body and the claim 6524736722; `Metadata-protocol: added` likewise.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6526285418 `open_questions`: `[]`. Nothing to escalate.
- Deviations (5), each answered: (a) file surface beyond the claim's two files — covered by claim amendment 6524793510 (data-engine.ts, protocol.ts, engine.ts) plus docblock/test/docs additions; none under `ui/**`, no governed path, no stored `sys_comment` field, no change to whom the gate admits — the claim's ⛔ lines hold. (b) sweep timing vs later commits — the derived set is CI's to confirm; the relevant families are among the in-progress runs. (c) worktree handling — process only. (d) `test:repo` not run locally — CI's (Test Core in progress). (e) a retried push — no residue in the tree.
- Out-of-scope findings (3): batch/clone/flow not answering — consistent with the ruling, carrier noted; non-author edit actor — taken up in ④ should-fix 3; the ui half card — the seat files it once the key is on `main`, as the ruling orders.
- Docs-drift bot (PR comment 6526283540): two changed files yielded no anchor (`api.json`, `hook-api.ts`). Read by hand: `api.json` is generated from 1 and `hook-api.ts` is a docblock word list over a type that already inherits the member. The two hand-written pages (`content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`, `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`) are not release-owned and state the rule as built (requester-only, ids only, omit-when-empty, update judges added mentions only).
- The maintainer's disclosure point (triage 6517777140) is answered by the ruling itself (accepted); the tree gives exactly the accepted bit — one id per user the requester named, no reason — and nothing wider (the gate's reason type is still only logged; the schema refuses any object per user).
- Pending gate families: the 22 in-progress check runs named in ①.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** — against ruling 6523848208 and its first consumers (`createData` / `updateData` → `crud-routes.ts` → `data-objectstack`). The member is where the ruling puts it (the data-write answer type), optional, ids only, one description for both answers so they cannot drift, and absent from the clone answer. Tried to break it: (i) a reason riding along — refused by `z.array(z.string())`; (ii) storage — `sys_comment` declares no such field and the answer is assembled from a per-call `Set`, never written (pinned against the real gate and SQLite: the stored row read back as system and as CAROL carries nothing); (iii) another request's answer — the set is local to the call and the listener rides the caller's own bag, so neither a nested hook write nor a sibling request can add to it (pinned in both test files). Holds. Two precision defects in the description, below.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`** — against its first consumer, the plugin-audit writer reading `ctx.input.options`, and against the protocol that passes it. The docblock's three claims were each verified in the engine: never called by the engine (no `onMentionsWithheld` reference in `engine.ts` outside the allowlist); reaches `after*` hooks on `ctx.input.options` through `buildDriverOptions`' additive widening (insert L15384–15396, update L16959, per-row contexts from the batch context); a throwing listener is caught and logged by the writer (`audit-writers.ts` L2612–2618). The consumer calls it once per written comment and only when at least one id was withheld (L2613), so a listener never sees an empty list. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts`** — a one-line docblock list; the type `HookUpdateOptions` already carries the member through `WriteObservabilityOptions`. Holds; nothing to break.

**Cited code the hits make claims about** (read, not reviewed; findings named where they bear on the contract):

- `mention-recipient-gate.ts`: the verdict path is unchanged; `onWithheld` fires after the log line, only with a resolved id, inside try/catch. The ruling's "gate's verdict reused" holds literally.
- `audit-writers.ts`: the writer dedups the ids and calls the write's own listener before emitting; on update it diffs against `ctx.previous`, so a kept mention is neither re-judged nor re-told (pinned). The messaging `dedupKey` `collab.mention:${commentId}:${uid}` additionally stops a double notification should a kept mention ever be re-spelled (email on create, id on edit) — belt and braces, not a gap.
- `comment-access-hooks.ts` L18–30: the `sys_comment` `beforeUpdate` rule admits the comment's **author or a holder of EDIT on the parent record**. This is what makes should-fix 3 reachable.
- `resolveMentionedUser` L285–304: any non-email token is taken as a user id without an existence read, so a mention of a non-existent id is judged (`cannot_read_source`) and reported back in `withheldMentions`. The PR body says such an entry "has no id to give back"; the tree does give it back. Harmless under the ruling — the requester typed the token, and user existence is already readable through the picker's `sys_user` directory read — but the PR body's account is wrong on this point. Observation, no fix owed.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix 1** — `protocol.zod.ts` `WRITE_ANSWER_WITHHELD_MENTIONS_DESCRIPTION` and the `data-engine.ts` docblock overstate the cause and the recipient. They say the ids were withheld "because they cannot read the comment or its record", but `withhold()` reports every reason that has a resolved user — `no_source_record`, `no_comment_id`, `source_record_missing`, `grants_unavailable` as well as the two readability reasons — and they say "the author is told", while on an update the answer goes to the requester, who may be a parent-record editor (above). The fact conveyed ("will not be notified") stays true in every case, so this is wording, not behaviour; but the description is the contract text the ui half will quote. Say "whose mention notification the gate withheld" and "the requester".

**Should-fix 2** — `packages/client/src/index.ts` `CreateDataResult` / `UpdateDataResult` (declared as mirrors of the two schemas) lack `withheldMentions?: string[]`. The wire carries the key and `data-objectstack` reads answers structurally, so nothing is blocked, but the typed SDK surface now disagrees with the spec it names, and the ui card will otherwise have to cast. One line each plus a `@objectstack/client` `minor` changeset — this PR or a follow-up before the ui card.

**Should-fix 3** — `audit-writers.ts` `writeCommentMentions` on `afterUpdate` keeps `actorId = row.author_id` and `actorName = row.author_name`. For the accepted scenario (the author edits their own comment) that is correct. For an edit by a parent-record editor (admitted by `comment-access-hooks.ts`), the new notifications are titled "{author} mentioned you" for a mention the editor added, and the author-skip excludes the wrong person. This path did not exist before (edits notified nobody), so it is new behaviour of this PR, not an inherited shape. `ctx.session.userId` is already read into `sess` two lines above; on the update branch use it as the actor when present. The dev report names the case; it should be closed here or on a card with a pointer, not left as a note.

Observations (no fix owed under the ruling): when the gate throws, no gate or no `messaging` is composed, or `emit` fails for an admitted user, nothing is told and the warn line is the only trace — the ruling scopes the member to the gate's verdict, and the PR says so; the stale "on `afterInsert`" comment at `audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts` L485–486 is the lane seat's.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-z0obcm`
Reviewed-by: `fable-subagent-of-session_01L9qibx5r5nhDMwpRs4SL6D`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `51450e766c971ee903fccf2cfb3c5b3a2188f5d7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mention-recipient-gate.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, .changeset/27703-withheld-mentions-answer.md (cited, read to judge; not reviewed)

Delta review of record 6526608625 (PASS on `9a38b6c0296098d1b52a9c09482f3a7ed4f36483`). Judged: the two patch commits `be32a8da` and `51450e76` (`git diff 9a38b6c0…51450e76`: 9 files, +72/−24), the updated PR body, and the check runs on `51450e76`. Everything the first record found right is carried forward unchanged unless named below; the delta touches no transport, gate-verdict or schema-shape line.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `WRITE_ANSWER_WITHHELD_MENTIONS_DESCRIPTION` (`protocol.zod.ts`) now says "WITHHELD by the mention recipient gate, so they will not be notified" and "the requester's own answer … the requester is told". **Right** — the causal clause and the recipient now match what `withhold()` reports (every reason with a resolved id) and who `comment-access-hooks.ts` admits to edit (author or parent-record editor). The schema shape (`z.array(z.string()).optional()`) is untouched, so no accept-set moves; the `write-answer-withheld-mentions.test.ts` pins (`/never stored/`, `/never the reason/`, both descriptions equal) still match the new text. `protocol.mdx` regenerated with the identical sentence on both rows. Should-fix 1 of 6526608625: **landed.**
2. `data-engine.ts` docblock: "the users the writer named … whatever the gate's reason (most often that they cannot read …) … on the requester's own answer". **Right**; same correction, type unchanged. Should-fix 1: **landed.**
3. `packages/client/src/index.ts`: `CreateDataResult` and `UpdateDataResult` gain `withheldMentions?: string[]` with a docblock in the style of the `warnings` member; `CloneDataResult` untouched, mirroring the schemas. **Right.** `@objectstack/client: minor` added to the changeset. Should-fix 2 of 6526608625: **landed.**
4. `audit-writers.ts` `writeCommentMentions`: on `afterUpdate` the actor is `ctx.session.userId` when present, else `row.author_id`; `actorName` stays `row.author_name` when the editor is the author, otherwise it is read through `resolveActorSnapshot(ctx.api, editorId).name` when `api.sudo` exists, else `null`. **Right**, and verified against the engine: the by-id update context carries `session: buildSession(opCtx.context)` and `api: buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` (engine.ts L16490–16510), per-row contexts are built from that batch context; `resolveActorSnapshot` is the existing actor reader (L1759), cached 30 s and wrapped in `.catch(() => NO_ACTOR_SNAPSHOT)`, so it cannot throw out of the hook and fail the edit; `buildHookApi` returns a `ScopedContext`, which has `sudo()`. On insert nothing changes (`editorId` is `null` outside `afterUpdate`). Should-fix 3 of 6526608625: **landed.**
5. New integration case "an edit by someone other than the author makes the EDITOR the actor": CAROL edits ALICE's comment adding `[ALICE, CAROL, BOB]`; expects audience `[[ALICE]]`, `actorId: CAROL`, `payload.actorName: CAROL.id`, `told: [[BOB]]`. **Right as a pin of the writer**: the fixture inserts every `sys_user` with `name: u.id`, so the title-field read yields `CAROL.id`; ALICE (the author) is a recipient, CAROL (the editor) is skipped, BOB (ORG_B) is withheld and told to CAROL's own listener. Note (not a defect): the harness composes no security or sharing service, so `canEditParent` falls to `sharingAndMasterAdmit` (comment-access-hooks.ts L734–739) and CAROL's edit is admitted by the degraded parent-read path, not by a real EDIT grant — the case pins the writer's actor rule, not the admission rule, which is what it claims to pin.
